reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
reports.description: Seychelles's national CPI. NBS's own CPI page describes it as measuring "changes in the price of goods and services actually charged to consumers," classified using UN COICOP ("12 divisions and four sub-group levels"), with a weight base period of 2018 (from the 2018 Household Budget Survey, covering Mahé, Praslin, La Digue) and a price base of 2020=100 introduced January 2021. A July 2024 IMF Technical Assistance mission on Seychelles's CPI (report title: "Report on Consumer Price Index Mission") states its aim was to ensure "the CPI more broadly reflects the standards and best practices described in the 2020 CPI Manual" — independent corroboration of active methodological modernisation, though this is IMF's own document about Seychelles, not NBS's self-published statement. A confirmed 2025/2026 primary NBS release was not directly verified this round (only third-party data-aggregator figures), though the TA mission and existing infrastructure strongly suggest continued monthly publication.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly per NBS's own site description; a specific 2025/2026 primary release was not independently re-verified this round.

_dropped.why: A SADC Secretariat HCPI bulletin (sadc.int/file/3171) lists Seychelles by name among covered member states and separately notes "Seychelles did not participate in the 2005 ICP round hence there is no Household Final Monetary Consumption Expenditure data (HFMCE) which are used as country weights for HCPI compilation" — real, specific evidence that Seychelles IS covered by the SADC HCPI. However: (1) this bulletin's specific URL and date could not be confirmed this round (the document appears undated, possibly a 2013-era edition, distinct from the originally-minted sadc-hcpi-newsletter node's Stage_1_HCPI PDF), and (2) NBS Seychelles's own site links to "SADC HCPI" only as a bare navigation hyperlink with no citing sentence, insufficient to quote. Deferred pending a dated, re-verified source rather than force-linked on an unverified/undated document, matching the caution applied to Mauritius's near-identical near-miss this same wave.
No NBS Seychelles document mentioning COMESA was located this round.

Seychelles is a founding member of the Indian Ocean Commission (COI/IOC), alongside Comoros, Madagascar, and Mauritius — all four founding members have now been researched in this branch and NONE has produced a citable COI/IOC document from their own statistics agency. This corpus's "no country cites the COI/IOC" gap remains open after exhausting the most likely candidates; a future session should consider searching the COI/IOC's OWN site for a document naming its member states' statistical cooperation, rather than continuing to search member states' sites individually.

GENUINE STRUCTURAL ABSENCE, not a search failure: Seychelles has 26 administrative districts with NO independent fiscal tier. Article 167 of the 1993 Constitution states "laws may provide for local government," but per a University of Pretoria academic country report, "this provision has not been fully implemented through new legislation," and "The Local Government Act of 1991 was suspended in 1993 when the current Constitution was promulgated." A Commonwealth Local Government Forum (CLGF) profile independently corroborates: "There is no constitutional provision for, or legislation governing, local government" and "The local administration has no powers to raise revenue and all funds are transferred from central government" (local government expenditure was 0.6% of total government expenditure in 2013/14). Both sources are secondary/academic (not a directly-verified primary Constitution quote — both the gov.sc PDF and constituteproject.org fetches of Article 167 failed or were truncated this round), so no node is minted for an absence; recorded here as a note for corpus completeness.
